correctness.rationale: For n>=1 and distinct strictly positive generator magnitudes, rearrangement gives a signed type-B Weyl chamber normal cone with n prefix-sum rays. A beam illuminates a vertex iff every prefix of a corresponding signed permutation is negative. Berger–Béthencourt applies exactly because a generic direction induces a finite exchangeable, sign-invariant sequence with nonvanishing partial sums; probability binom(2n,n)/4^n times 2^n n! gives (2n-1)!!. Strict-inequality perturbation bounds non-generic beams. Group orbit averaging gives I*=2^n n!/(2n-1)!!=4^n/binom(2n,n). Independently enumerated every signed permutation for n=1..6 and recovered 1,3,15,105,945,10395, not an all-rank substitute.
